Sensitivity Analysis for the Sample Size Planning Method for Standardized ANCOVA Contrast

Source: R/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.Rd

Sensitivity analysis for the sample size planning method with the goal to obtain sufficiently narrow confidence intervals for standardized ANCOVA complex contrasts.

Usage

ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity(
  true_std_contrast = NULL,
  supposed_std_contrast = NULL,
  c_weights,
  width = NULL,
  specified_n_per_group = NULL,
  true_mean_X = 0,
  true_sd_X = 1,
  true_cor,
  divisor = "s_ancova",
  assurance = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  G = 10000,
  print_iter = TRUE,
  filename = NULL,
  assurance_method = c("analytic", "simulation"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_std_contrast

the population standardized ANCOVA contrast

supposed_std_contrast

the supposed standardized ANCOVA contrast, the planning value given to ss_aipe_sc_ancova to choose the sample size

c_weights

the contrast weights

width

the desired full width of the obtained confidence interval. Required when supposed_std_contrast is given, because the sample size is planned from it; a call without it is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid.

specified_n_per_group

selected sample size per group to use in order to determine distributional properties of a given value of sample size

true_mean_X

the population mean for the covariate

true_sd_X

the population standard deviation of the covariate

true_cor

the population correlation coefficient between the response and the covariate

divisor

which error standard deviation to be used in standardizing the contrast; the value can be either "s_ancova" or "s_anova"

assurance

parameter to ensure that the obtained confidence interval width is narrower than the desired width with a specified degree of certainty. When the sample size is planned from supposed_std_contrast, it is passed to ss_aipe_sc_ancova and must be NULL or greater than .5 and less than 1; with specified_n_per_group it is only reported in the result.

conf_level

the desired confidence interval coverage, (i.e., 1 - Type I error rate)

G

number of generations (i.e., replications) of the simulation

print_iter

to print the current value of the iterations

filename

Optional path of a CSV file to receive the per-replication results (the observed standardized contrast, std_contrast, the full and one-sided interval widths, the tail and overall misses, and the confidence limits), appended when the file already exists and created otherwise; the default NULL writes nothing, and a throwaway run that wants the file should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

assurance_method

Passed to ss_aipe_sc_ancova, which plans the sample size from supposed_std_contrast with assurance: "analytic" (the default) for the published plan of Lai and Kelley (2012), which does not compute the probability it attains and can attain less than assurance, and "simulation" for the smallest sample size per group at which the probability of an interval no wider than width, estimated by the planner from its default G of 10000 simulated samples with the random number stream that seed sets, is at least assurance. Not used with specified_n_per_group or without assurance.

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value summarizing the Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis across G replications. The term entries are: mean_std_contrast, median_std_contrast, sd_std_contrast (summaries of the realized standardized ANCOVA contrast); mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, sd_ci_width (summaries of the full interval widths); mean_ci_width_lower and mean_ci_width_upper (mean one-sided widths, measured from the observed contrast to each limit); pct_ci_less_width (proportion of intervals at or below the target width); pct_ci_miss_low and pct_ci_miss_high (tail-specific empirical non-coverage of true_std_contrast); total_type_I_error (overall empirical non-coverage, the sum of the two tails); and the input echoes n_per_group (the size simulated at, planned or specified), total_N, true_std_contrast, supposed_std_contrast (NA when specified_n_per_group was supplied instead), true_cor, width, conf_level, and assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied). The proportion and Type I error rows are proportions on the 0 to 1 scale, not percentages.

Details

The sample size planning method this function is based on is developed in the context of simple (i.e., one-response-one-covariate) ANCOVA model and randomized design (i.e., same population covariate mean across groups).

An ANCOVA contrast can be standardized in at least two ways: (a) divided by the error standard deviation of the ANOVA model, (b) divided by the error standard deviation of the ANCOVA model. This function can be used to analyze both types of standardized ANCOVA contrasts.

The population mean and standard deviation of the covariate does not affect the sample size planning procedure; they can be specified as any values that are considered as reasonable by the user.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K. (2007). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Lai, K., & Kelley, K. (2012). Accuracy in parameter estimation for ANCOVA and ANOVA contrasts: Sample size planning via narrow confidence intervals. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 65, 350–370. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.2011.02029.x

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 9.)

Steiger, J. H., & Fouladi, R. T. (1997). Noncentrality interval estimation and the evaluation of statistical models. In L. L. Harlow, S. A. Mulaik, & J. H. Steiger (Eds.), What if there were no significance tests? (pp. 221–257). Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

See also

ss_aipe_sc_ancova, ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Sensitivity analysis for a standardized ANCOVA contrast across
# three groups, contrast (-1, 0, 1), a covariate-outcome correlation
# of 0.4, and a planning target width of 0.5. G = 50 keeps the
# example quick; a reported sensitivity analysis deserves the default of
# G = 10000 replications.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity(
  true_std_contrast = 0.5, supposed_std_contrast = 0.5,
  c_weights = c(-1, 0, 1),
  width = 0.5, true_cor = 0.4,
  conf_level = 0.95, G = 50, print_iter = FALSE
)
#>  term                  value
#>  mean_std_contrast     0.481
#>  median_std_contrast   0.467
#>  sd_std_contrast       0.119
#>  mean_ci_width         0.500
#>  median_ci_width       0.499
#>  sd_ci_width           0.002
#>  mean_ci_width_lower   0.250
#>  mean_ci_width_upper   0.249
#>  pct_ci_less_width     0.580
#>  pct_ci_miss_low       0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_high      0.020
#>  total_type_I_error    0.020
#>  n_per_group           126  
#>  total_N               378  
#>  true_std_contrast     0.500
#>  supposed_std_contrast 0.500
#>  true_cor              0.400
#>  width                 0.500
#>  conf_level            0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 50
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
